findings.explanation: Splunkbase 4856 is the community 'Metrics Add-on for Infrastructure' and 1810 is 'Hunk App for MongoDB'. The Splunk Add-on for VMware is 3215; NSX integrations on Splunkbase are the VMware NSX-T Splunk App (4241) and TA-nsx (6805). The same IDs recur in detailedImplementation and references.
findings.suggested_fix: Use Splunk Add-on for VMware (3215) and a real NSX integration (4241/6805) or describe the Edge feeds as custom collectors.

findings.explanation: The Splunk Add-on for VMware has no `vmware:vmware:vsphere:vcenter` sourcetype; Edge VM sizing would come from `vmware:inv:vm`. Repeated in detailedImplementation.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `vmware:inv:vm` for Edge VM sizing joins.

findings.explanation: BGP neighbor state, LB pool member status and IPSec SA counts are device/session state, not flow records; Network_Traffic requires src/dest/bytes/action tuples the SPL never produces. dataModelAcceleration repeats this by proposing to accelerate Network_Traffic on bgp_neighbor_state/pool_member_status.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep Performance (CPU, throughput) and drop Network_Traffic; remove the Network_Traffic acceleration guidance.

findings.explanation: The SPL raises `dpdk_drop_ratio_high` only when drops > 10000 AND pps > 50000 AND drops/pps > 0.01; CPU > 92 is a separate class. It also alerts on BGP, LB member, runtime, HA and VPN classes the description omits. controlTest repeats the OR wording.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe each edge_risk class and its actual condition (drops > 10000 and pps > 50000 and ratio > 1%; CPU > 92%; BGP not Established; member DOWN/DISABLED/...).

findings.explanation: No such edge-cluster sessions endpoint is known; IPSec session status/statistics are exposed under the Policy tier-0/tier-1 `locale-services/{ls}/ipsec-vpn-services/{svc}/sessions/{id}` paths. Similarly `lb-services/{lbs-id}/lb-pools/{pool-id}/members` in dataSources does not match the Policy LB status API shape.
findings.quote: Mirror `GET /api/v1/edge-clusters/{cluster-id}/sessions` feeds capturing `IKEv2` phase-1 / phase-2 counts
findings.suggested_fix: Check the NSX 4.2 Policy API reference for IPSec session statistics and LB pool status (e.g. `/policy/api/v1/infra/lb-services/{id}/lb-pools/{id}/detailed-status`) and cite exact paths.

findings.explanation: The `BGP[NEIGHBOR]:` / `lb[VIRTUAL_SERVER]:` message tokens and the `/var/log/edgexb/` path are not documented NSX Edge log formats; the SPL syslog filter depends on them. The alarm names `EDGE_NODE_DOWN`, `BGP_NEIGHBOR_DOWN` etc. and the Edge CLI `get dataplane stats` also need confirmation.
findings.quote: Edge /var/log/syslog (BGP[NEIGHBOR]:, lb[VIRTUAL_SERVER]:, ipsec[]:, charon) plus /var/log/edgexb/*.log structured exporters
findings.suggested_fix: Verify against NSX 4.2 Edge log reference and NSX alarm catalogue (event IDs such as routing / load_balancer / ipsec events) and the Edge nsxcli reference; replace with real tokens.

findings.explanation: Troubleshooting repeats itself ('Drops minus optics faults' and 'Drops with healthy optics'; 'Throughput dips during HA' and 'HA syslog storms') and has a doubled-markdown typo (`****vmware:nsxt:edge_bgp****`).
findings.quote: • **Drops with healthy optics** — Escalate NIC driver regressions
findings.suggested_fix: Merge duplicate bullets and fix the markdown.

findings.explanation: Reference points to the techdocs home page, not the Edge cluster chapter.
findings.suggested_fix: Link the NSX 4.2 Administration Guide Edge cluster page.

findings.explanation: Marked verified by an automated agent despite wrong add-on IDs and a base search that cannot run as written.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade status until a human SME validates against a live NSX Edge feed.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: Base search contains `(sourcetype="vmware:nsxt:syslog" AND match(lower(_raw),"..."))`; `match()`/`lower()` are eval functions and are not valid inside the implicit `search` command. Use `| where match(...)` or `| regex` after retrieval.

Numeric fields are coalesced to "0", so `isnotnull(dataplane_drops)` is always true and `ipsec_tunnel_count==0` fires for any edge_vpn event missing the count field; the `edge_ha_cluster_event` regex also matches any line containing 'bfd'.

Title promises 'Load-Balancer Pool Capacity' and gateway throughput, but the SPL only checks pool member status and throughput peaks inside rows already flagged for another reason; no capacity metric (connections, pool utilisation) is evaluated.

summary: The Edge risk taxonomy (BGP not established, LB member down, DPDK drop ratio, HA events, empty VPN inventory) is useful, but the add-on identities are wrong, the base search uses an eval function, Network_Traffic is a poor CIM fit, several NSX API paths/CLI commands/log tokens look invented, and the description states the drop thresholds as OR when the SPL requires all of them.
